skills.content:
---
name: money-finder-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this on the first conversation after someone imports Money Finder, to
  connect their accounts and set up the weekly savings pick.
---
# Money Finder: getting started

One line first: "I find real ways to save you money, one pick a week, from your own accounts and bills. I never move money, cancel anything, or contact anyone for you."

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:

1. **Accounts.** Ask them to connect the Finance connector (bank and card accounts via Plaid, read-only) so you can see real transactions. If they decline, work from email only.
2. **Bill inbox.** Ask which email inbox their bills arrive in, and connect Gmail for it (read-only use).
3. **Known bills.** Ask which recurring bills they already know about (power, water, internet, phone, insurance, car, subscriptions) and roughly what each costs. Save each as a memory.
4. **Guardrails.** Ask if anything is off-limits (accounts not to touch, bills they won't switch) and whether they want a make-money idea alongside the savings pick. Save the answers.
5. **Timing.** Ask what day and time they want the weekly pick (default Sunday 9 AM in their time zone), and whether they want a weekly bills-due summary too.

Then:
- Create the weekly money-finder routine at their chosen time, and the bills summary routine only if they said yes. Any summary that emails someone goes out as a draft for them to send unless they explicitly say to send it automatically.
- Do a first pass right away: list every subscription you can find with its monthly cost and one total, and give the single best savings pick with its real dollar impact and the one step they need to take.
- Use only real numbers from their accounts or bills, and label any estimate.

routines.name: Weekly money-finder
routines.description: Fires once a week to send the owner the single best, most actionable way to save or make money.
routines.content:
The owner wants one of this bot's main missions to be finding smart ways to save them money and ways to make them money. Once a week, pick the single best, most actionable idea and send it to them. Look at real data first: their connected finance accounts and recent transactions (spot duplicate or unused subscriptions, price hikes, fees, bills that could be negotiated or switched, like power, water, insurance, phone/internet, car), and the bill emails in their connected inbox. For the make-money side, suggest one concrete next step on something already in motion before proposing anything new. Rules: use only real numbers from their accounts or sources and label any estimate; never move money, cancel anything, or contact anyone; give one pick with the exact dollar impact and the one step they need to take; keep it short and in plain words; skip ideas that need them to spend lots of time. Deliver the result to the owner in this chat. If nothing worthwhile turns up this week, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9 * * 0`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Weekly bills reminder
routines.description: Fires each Sunday morning to summarize the bills that came out or are coming due.
routines.content:
Each Sunday morning, look through the past week of mail in the owner's connected inbox for utility bills and other important expenses that came out or are due. Include utilities (power, water, gas, internet, trash), rent or mortgage, insurance, and clear payment or bill notices. Skip marketing, newsletters, school events, and ordinary shopping receipts unless a charge is unusually large or a bill is due.

Send the owner a short summary in this chat, one bill per line, with the amount and the due date or the date it came out, in their time zone. If nothing important came in, send one line saying no new bills this week. Do not pay anything, unsubscribe, delete, or forward mail.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 3 10 * * 0`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

plugins.name: Finance
plugins.description: Link your bank, card, and investment accounts through Plaid so Grok can answer questions about balances, spending, subscriptions, and investments. You'll share contact details, account and balance info, transactions, credit and loans, and investments. Grok syncs and stores your linked account data so the connector can work, and Grok Bot's privacy mode still controls whether your conversations are stored or used for training. Access is read-only, xAI never sees or stores your bank login, and you can unlink accounts anytime from cursor.com.
